subject: maths
title: Percentages of Amounts
welcome_lead: Find a percentage of any amount with quick mental tricks and reliable methods.
meta_desc: Learn to find percentages of amounts and percentage changes in this KS3 adventure.
final_note: Brilliant! Percentage problems hold no fear now.

concepts.def: A decimal used to scale a quantity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
% change = (change ÷ original) × 100.

If price rises from £40 to £50, change = £10. % change = (10 ÷ 40) × 100 = 25%.

mcqs.q: Is the result of 8 x 0.4 larger or smaller than 8?
options: Larger, because multiplying always makes numbers bigger.
Smaller — multiplying by a number between 0 and 1 makes the result smaller (the answer is 3.2).
The same as 8, because 0.4 is too small to change anything.
